scope: Named fictional or legendary maritime characters and a separate selection of 25 well-known historical explorers, sailors and mariners, with additional pools for related sea figures and advertising mascots. Broad initial catalogue, not exhaustive.

entries.name: Ancaeus
entries.note: The son of Poseidon in Apollonius; ancient accounts differ and include another Ancaeus.

entries.name: Argus
entries.note: The Argo builder; parentage and identification vary across ancient accounts.

entries.name: Bran mac Febail
entries.note: Distinct from Bran the Blessed in Welsh tradition.

entries.name: Brendan the Navigator
entries.note: A historical saint with a legendary voyage tradition; not simply an invented fictional character.

entries.name: Hendrick van der Decken
entries.note: One named version of the captain; names and details vary between retellings. The Flying Dutchman is generally the ship.

entries.name: Neptune
entries.note: Roman counterpart of Poseidon; kept separate because these are distinct named cultural traditions.

entries.name: Njörðr
entries.role: God associated with seafaring and fishing

entries.name: Rán
entries.role: Sea figure associated with the drowned

entries.name: Leif Erikson
entries.note: Voyaged to Vinland in North America.

entries.name: Zheng He
entries.note: Commanded treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean.

entries.name: Christopher Columbus
entries.work_or_tradition: Atlantic voyages for the Crown of Castile
entries.note: Led four transatlantic voyages beginning in 1492.

entries.name: Amerigo Vespucci
entries.note: Explored the South American coast; the Americas were named after him.

entries.name: Bartolomeu Dias
entries.note: Rounded the southern tip of Africa in 1488.

entries.name: Vasco da Gama
entries.note: Led the 1497–1499 voyage from Portugal to India around Africa.

entries.name: John Cabot
entries.note: Sailed west from Bristol seeking a route to Asia.

entries.name: Ferdinand Magellan
entries.note: Began the 1519–1522 expedition; died before Elcano and the remaining crew completed the circumnavigation.

entries.name: Juan Sebastián Elcano
entries.note: Commanded Victoria on the return to Spain that completed the expedition’s circumnavigation in 1522.

entries.name: Jacques Cartier
entries.note: Explored the Gulf and River of St. Lawrence.

entries.name: Francis Drake
entries.note: Completed a circumnavigation in 1577–1580.

entries.name: Henry Hudson
entries.note: Sought northern sea passages to Asia.

entries.name: Abel Tasman
entries.note: Led voyages to Tasmania and New Zealand and surveyed northern Australia.

entries.name: James Cook
entries.note: Led three Pacific exploration voyages.

entries.name: George Vancouver
entries.note: Surveyed the Pacific coast of North America during the 1791–1795 expedition.

entries.name: Jeanne Baret
entries.work_or_tradition: Bougainville expedition and subsequent return voyage
entries.note: Recognized as the first woman to complete a circumnavigation of the globe.

entries.name: Fridtjof Nansen
entries.note: Led the first Fram expedition in an attempt to reach the North Pole.

entries.name: Roald Amundsen
entries.note: Led the first expedition to navigate the Northwest Passage.

entries.name: Ernest Shackleton
entries.note: Led the Endurance expedition and the James Caird boat journey to South Georgia.

entries.name: Joshua Slocum
entries.note: Completed the first recorded solo sailing circumnavigation in 1895–1898.

entries.name: Jacques-Yves Cousteau
entries.role: Research vessel captain and ocean explorer
entries.note: Conducted ocean expeditions aboard Calypso.

entries.name: Thor Heyerdahl
entries.note: Led the 1947 Kon-Tiki raft voyage from Peru to Polynesia.

entries.name: Francis Chichester
entries.work_or_tradition: Solo circumnavigation aboard Gipsy Moth IV
entries.note: Circumnavigated solo in 1966–1967 with a stop in Sydney.

entries.name: Robin Knox-Johnston
entries.role: Merchant navy officer and solo sailor
entries.note: Completed the first solo nonstop sailing circumnavigation in 1968–1969.

entries.name: Ellen MacArthur
entries.note: Set a solo circumnavigation speed record in 2005.

boundary_notes.name: Kupe
boundary_notes.reason: Māori oral histories describe an exploring ancestor; do not classify him as an invented character.

boundary_notes.name: Blackbeard / Edward Teach; Anne Bonny; Mary Read; Ching Shih; William Kidd
boundary_notes.decision: not yet selected for historical pool
boundary_notes.reason: Historical pirates outside the current 25-person historical selection. Francis Drake and Zheng He now have separate historical records; fictional adaptations still require explicitly identified records.

boundary_notes.name: Captain Kirk; Jean-Luc Picard; Captain Harlock; Malcolm Reynolds
boundary_notes.reason: Spacefaring captains without a central waterborne role.

boundary_notes.name: Master Bates; Seaman Staines; Roger the Cabin Boy
boundary_notes.reason: Not the characters in Captain Pugwash; use Master Mate and Tom the Cabin Boy.

boundary_notes.name: Flying Dutchman
boundary_notes.decision: not a separate default person entry
boundary_notes.reason: Usually a ship name; use the specifically identified captain, such as Van der Decken.

boundary_notes.name: Davy Jones — sailors’ folklore
boundary_notes.decision: represented by a specific film adaptation above
boundary_notes.reason: The folklore figure and the Pirates of the Caribbean captain should not be treated as interchangeable biographies.

historical_selection.basis: Editorial selection of widely known maritime explorers and sailors across early ocean voyages, polar exploration, ocean research and solo sailing. Not a measured popularity ranking.
